llm.summary: The skill's behavior mostly matches its stated purpose (scanning local session JSONL and scheduling resume jobs), but the installer references missing template files and the install/auto-resume behavior (writing systemd drop-ins and scheduling system-event cron jobs that will re-run agent actions) deserves careful review before installing.

dimensions.detail: The skill claims to detect interrupted OpenClaw sessions and schedule resume events; it requires python3 and the openclaw CLI and reads ~/.openclaw session files — all of which are coherent with session-resume functionality.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions and the script only read OpenClaw agent session/index files and then call 'openclaw cron add --system-event' to inject a continuation prompt. That is within scope, but it does read potentially sensitive conversation contents and will autonomously schedule jobs that can re-trigger tool executions; users should understand that resumed jobs may re-run operations the agent was performing before the crash.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Installer is local and conservative (copies script into the workspace and writes user systemd drop-ins) — no external downloads — but install.sh references templates under 'templates/' (boot-resume.conf and boot-resume-wake.service) that are not present in the provided file manifest. This mismatch can break installation or hide omitted files; additionally, the installer enables a user systemd service which is a persistent system change and should be reviewed.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no credentials or external secrets. It optionally honors OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR and otherwise operates on files under the user's ~/.openclaw directory, which is proportional to the stated goal.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill installs a systemd drop-in and a user service and will schedule cron jobs that autonomously invoke the agent (normal for resume behavior). 'always' is false, but the persistent systemd changes and autonomous cron scheduling increase the blast radius if misused; this is expected for its purpose but worth conscious consent.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
What to check before installing:
- Review the actual scripts (scripts/boot-resume-check.sh) line-by-line to confirm you understand what it reads and what resume prompt it will inject. The script reads your session JSONL files and will schedule 'openclaw cron add --system-event' jobs that can cause the agent to re-run operations.
- The installer refers to templates/boot-resume.conf and templates/boot-resume-wake.service but these files are not present in the provided manifest; verify the package includes those templates or be prepared to supply safe drop-in files yourself.
- Installing modifies your ~/.config/systemd/user and enables a user service — if you prefer manual control, copy the script yourself and run it with '--no-wait' to test behavior before enabling automatic triggers.
- Run the script manually in a safe environment first (bash scripts/boot-resume-check.sh --no-wait) and inspect /tmp/openclaw/boot-resume.log to see what would be resumed.
- If you are concerned about unintended side effects, backup ~/.openclaw workspace and consider restricting the scan window or disabling automatic systemd drop-in deployment.
- If anything looks unexpected (resume jobs for sessions you don't expect, references to missing templates), do not enable/enable the service and ask the skill author for the missing files and an explanation.
